title: VPC Exam Drill
intro: Twelve scenario questions on subnets, routing, NAT, endpoints and the stateful/stateless pair. Answer cold — the explanation appears after each choice.
footer: Drawn from Lab 01 — VPC from scratch. Reference notes: exam-notes.md
notes_intro: Twelve SAA-C03-style questions drawn from what this lab builds, then the traps and the reference tables worth memorising. Answers are at the bottom — try them cold first.

questions.q: An EC2 instance launches into a subnet with an auto-assigned public IPv4 address. Its security group allows all outbound traffic and the subnet uses the default network ACL. The instance still cannot reach the internet. What is the most likely cause?
options: The instance needs an Elastic IP instead of an auto-assigned public IP
The subnet's route table has no 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway
The instance needs a NAT gateway to reach the internet
DNS hostnames are disabled on the VPC
questions.why: A public IP does nothing on its own. A subnet is public only because its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway — that route is the entire definition. An Elastic IP changes nothing when a public IP is already assigned, a NAT gateway serves instances without public IPs, and DNS hostnames affect name resolution rather than reachability.

questions.q: Instances in a private subnet cannot complete outbound HTTPS requests — connections hang and time out. The security group allows TCP 443 outbound. A custom network ACL allows TCP 443 outbound, and inbound allows all traffic from 10.0.0.0/16 only. What fixes it?
options: Add an inbound rule for TCP 443 to the security group
Add an inbound network ACL rule allowing TCP 1024–65535 from 0.0.0.0/0
Add an outbound rule for ephemeral ports to the security group
Replace the custom network ACL with the default network ACL
questions.why: Network ACLs are stateless — each packet is evaluated in each direction independently. The reply to an outbound HTTPS request arrives as a new inbound packet on an ephemeral port (1024–65535) and needs its own rule. The security group needs nothing because it is stateful. Replacing the ACL would work but discards the intended subnet controls.

questions.q: Private instances download several terabytes per month from Amazon S3, currently routed through a NAT gateway. Which change reduces cost the most?
options: Create an interface endpoint for S3
Create a gateway endpoint for S3
Move the instances to a public subnet
Add a second NAT gateway to spread the load
questions.why: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free, and remove both the NAT hourly cost and the $0.0059/GB data processing charge for that traffic. An interface endpoint also bypasses NAT but bills hourly and per GB. Moving to a public subnet breaks the security posture; a second NAT increases cost.

questions.q: A security policy forbids any internet path from a private subnet — no NAT gateway, no internet gateway route. Administrators must still get an interactive shell via Session Manager. Which VPC interface endpoints are required?
options: ssm only
ssm and ec2
ssm, ssmmessages and ec2messages
ssm, ssmmessages and s3
questions.why: All three are needed: ssm for the service API, ssmmessages for the Session Manager data channel, and ec2messages for the agent's command channel. Miss any one and the instance never shows as managed. An S3 gateway endpoint is needed only if you want session logs written to S3.

questions.q: One NAT gateway sits in the public subnet of AZ-a. Private subnets in both AZ-a and AZ-b share a single route table pointing at it. AZ-a suffers a full outage. What happens to instances in AZ-b's private subnet?
options: They continue normally; NAT gateways are regional
They lose outbound internet connectivity
They automatically fail over to an internet gateway
They lose all connectivity, including to other subnets in the VPC
questions.why: A NAT gateway is zonal, not regional. A single NAT is a single point of failure for every private subnet routed through it — and in normal operation AZ-b's traffic also pays a cross-AZ transfer charge. The resilient pattern is one NAT per AZ with a route table per AZ. Intra-VPC traffic keeps working via the local route.

questions.q: How many usable IP addresses does a 10.20.11.0/24 subnet provide for EC2 instances?
questions.why: A /24 holds 256 addresses and AWS reserves five in every subnet: network (.0), VPC router (.1), DNS (.2), reserved for future use (.3), and broadcast (.255). That leaves 251. The tempting wrong answer is 254 — the on-premises networking answer.

questions.q: Two VPCs must exchange traffic. VPC-A uses 10.0.0.0/16 and VPC-B uses 10.0.0.0/24. What is the outcome of creating a VPC peering connection?
options: It succeeds; the more specific route wins
It succeeds, but only one direction works
It fails — peered VPCs cannot have overlapping CIDR blocks
It succeeds if a transit gateway is used instead
questions.why: Peered VPCs cannot have overlapping or matching CIDR blocks; the request fails outright. A transit gateway does not solve it either. This is why CIDR planning matters before you build — it cannot be changed later without a rebuild, and it is exactly why this lab chose 10.20.0.0/16.

questions.q: Instances with only IPv6 addresses in a private subnet need to download OS updates from the internet, but nothing on the internet may initiate a connection to them. What provides this?
options: A NAT gateway
An egress-only internet gateway
An internet gateway with a restrictive network ACL
A NAT instance with source/destination checking disabled
questions.why: An egress-only internet gateway is the IPv6 counterpart to a NAT gateway: outbound-only, stateful, horizontally scaled and free. NAT gateways and NAT instances handle IPv4 only. IPv6 addresses are globally routable, so a plain internet gateway would leave the instances inbound-reachable.

questions.q: A security team enables VPC Flow Logs at the VPC level with TrafficType: ALL. Which traffic will not appear in the logs?
options: Rejected inbound SSH attempts
Traffic between two instances in different subnets of the same VPC
Requests to the instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254
Outbound HTTPS traffic to the internet through a NAT gateway
questions.why: Flow logs exclude traffic to the instance metadata service, the Amazon DNS server, DHCP, Windows license activation, and the reserved VPC router address. They do capture rejected traffic, intra-VPC traffic, and NAT-bound traffic — the ACCEPT/REJECT field is your evidence of which control dropped a packet.

questions.q: A single malicious IP address is attacking a public-facing application. The team wants to block that one address at the subnet boundary while allowing all other traffic. What should they use?
options: A security group inbound deny rule
A network ACL inbound deny rule
A security group with the IP removed from the allow list
An egress-only internet gateway
questions.why: Security groups support allow rules only — there is no deny. Blocking a specific source requires a network ACL, which supports allow and deny and is evaluated in rule-number order, lowest first, first match wins. Any exam question about blocking one IP is a NACL question.

questions.q: A workload requires that the device performing network address translation be protected by a security group, and that the same device also serve as a bastion host. Which option meets both requirements?
options: A NAT gateway
A NAT instance
An egress-only internet gateway
An internet gateway
questions.why: A NAT instance is an ordinary EC2 instance, so it can carry a security group and double as a bastion. A NAT gateway supports neither — only the subnet's network ACL applies to it. The trade-off is that NAT instances need manual HA, patching, and source/destination checking disabled.

questions.q: A development VPC has a NAT gateway that processes essentially no traffic outside business hours. The team is surprised by the monthly bill. Why?
options: NAT gateways bill per connection, and idle connections still count
NAT gateways bill an hourly charge regardless of traffic, plus a per-GB data processing charge
The Elastic IP is billed at a premium when attached to a NAT gateway
NAT gateways bill a minimum of 1 TB of data processing per month
questions.why: A NAT gateway bills roughly $0.059/hour whether or not a single packet crosses it — about $43/month idle — plus $0.0059 per GB processed. It is the most common cause of surprise charges in a personal AWS account, and the reason this lab verifies teardown with a tag sweep instead of trusting DELETE_COMPLETE.
